# How to read this cookbook {#sec-how-to-read .unnumbered}

This is a chef's cookbook, not the reference manual. Every recipe is one feature
on the same five-beat rhythm:

0. **This is a recipe for…** — what dish, and why you'd cook it.
1. **The DecL** — the program, pretty-printed, aiming to be self-explanatory.
2. **Build & validate** — `build`, then `.valid` and `.validation_explanation`.
3. **Exhibits** — `summary_df` / `stats_df` / `.plot()` / the relevant
   `*_explanation`.
4. **The check** — the invariant, made visible. This is the point: you *see* the
   thing the pytest suite asserts, so you can trust the suite.

Everything shares one calibrated *house book* (`_setup.py`, the single source of
truth for the example numbers) so the figures carry across pages. Each page also
runs standalone in JupyterLab — open any `_NN_*.qmd` and go.

The pricing background (distortions, bounds, allocation) follows
@Mildenhall2022a; the FFT compound-distribution engine follows @Mildenhall2024, which in turn was based on @Grubel1999.

**Organization.** Sections own a number; recipes within a section are `N.M`, so
adding an example never renumbers its neighbors.

```{python}
from _setup import *
version
```
